title: [Chapitre] VIII. Analysis situs (quatrième mouture) : notes manuscrites (26/06-04/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 41–44 of the manuscript). Grothendieck is axiomatising 'figures ensemblistes' (set-theoretic figures). These are purely combinatorial models of stratified spaces or cell complexes, inside the 1986 'Analysis situs' notes.

Setting:
- X is a set and (X_i)_{i∈I} is a family of subsets indexed by an ordered set I, with i≤j ⇒ X_i⊂X_j.
- The boundary is ∂X_i = ∪_{j<i} X_j.
- The 'open cell' is X_i^0 = X_i \ ∂X_i.

Corollary 3 (previous page) characterises when (X_i) is a figure indexed by I:
- (b') every X_i^0 ≠ ∅;
- (b'') X_i^0 ∩ X_j^0 = ∅ for i≠j;
- (c) for each i, the subfamily 𝔛_i = {X_j : j≤i} is itself a figure ensembliste in the intrinsic sense, i.e. indexed by the sets themselves, ordered by inclusion.

This page proves the key steps.

(1) Fix i. For j≤i, define the intrinsic open cell of X_j inside 𝔛_i as X_j^{0'} = X_j \ ∪{X_{j'} : j'≤i, X_{j'} ⊊ X_j}. Here j'≤j is not assumed. Grothendieck claims this union contains all the terms of the union defining X_j^0. That amounts to: j'<j ⇒ X_{j'} ≠ X_j. The proof runs as follows:
- X_{j'} ⊂ ∂X_j, so X_j \ X_{j'} ⊇ X_j \ ∂X_j = X_j^0.
- X_j^0 ≠ ∅ by (b').
- Hence X_{j'} ⊊ X_j.
Consequently X_j^{0'} ⊂ X_j^0.

(2) In a crossed-out passage, the argument continues:
- By (c), the intrinsic cells cover X_i, so ∪_{j≤i} X_j^{0'} = X_i.
- Also ∪_{j≤i} X_j^0 = X_i.
- Since the X_j^0 are non-empty and pairwise disjoint and X_j^{0'} ⊂ X_j^0, one gets X_j^{0'} = X_j^0.
So the intrinsic cells coincide with the indexed cells. This block was struck through, apparently because Grothendieck found a shorter route to what he needed.

(3) Restart (completed on the next page). The aim is to show the order is recovered from inclusion: X_i ⊂ X_j ⇒ i ≤ j. The proof:
- Take x ∈ X_i^0, which exists by (b').
- By (c) applied to 𝔛_j, there is j'≤j with x ∈ X_{j'}^{0'} ⊂ X_{j'}^0.
- So X_i^0 ∩ X_{j'}^0 ≠ ∅, and (b'') gives i = j' ≤ j.

Purpose: show that a figure indexed by an abstract poset is the same as one indexed intrinsically by its closed pieces. The poset I is then isomorphic to (the closed strata, ⊂), and the open strata partition each closed stratum. This is the set-theoretic skeleton of the face poset of a stratified space or regular cell complex, presumably preparing tame/combinatorial 'analysis situs'.
errors: No real mathematical error. The step X_{j'} ⊂ ∂X_j silently uses monotonicity of the indexing (j'≤j ⇒ X_{j'}⊂X_j), which is part of the standing definition.
The struck-out step 'X_j^{0'} = X_j^0' uses the covering ∪X_j^{0'} = X_i from (c) applied to 𝔛_i. This is correct: for x∈X_j^0, x lies in some X_k^{0'} ⊂ X_k^0, and disjointness forces k=j.
Minor wording slip: Grothendieck writes 'cette réunion comporte plus de termes' where he means 'at least as many terms', i.e. the index set contains that of the definition of X_j^0.

ideas.what: Cells of a poset-indexed family of closed sets: X_i^0 = X_i minus the union of smaller members; a figure is one where cells are non-empty, pairwise disjoint and cover each X_i
ideas.modern_name: Poset-stratified set / closure-finite stratification; face poset of a regular cell complex; strata of a stratification indexed by a poset
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Whitney/Thom stratifications; Alexandrov topology on posets; regular CW face posets). Poset-stratified spaces in Lurie's Higher Algebra appendix A and Ayala–Francis–Tanaka
ideas.where_published: Not in published texts; the 'figures' language appears only in the unpublished 1986 Analysis situs notes, and is related only in spirit to the tame topology programme of Esquisse §5–6

ideas.what: Recovery of the indexing order from inclusion of closed pieces, and independence of open cells from the indexing (intrinsic vs indexed cells)
ideas.modern_name: Face poset determined by closures of strata (frontier condition: X_i ⊂ X_j iff i ≤ j)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore / frontier condition in stratification theory

deep.surprise_reason: Careful but elementary set-theoretic lemma: indexed cells equal intrinsic cells, and the order is recovered from inclusion. It belongs to a foundational axiomatisation of combinatorial stratified sets. It is of documentary interest for the 1986 Analysis situs project, but the mathematics is routine and well known in substance.
transcription_corrections: Line 2: 'cellule ouverte de X_j dans 𝔛_i' (script X, the subfamily 𝔛_i), not '𝔏_i'.
Marginal NB: 'NB dans cette réunion, on ne suppose pas j'≤j' ('réunion' rather than 'sommaire'). Likewise 'Cette réunion comporte plus de termes que celle analogue qui figure dans la déf. de X_j^0'.
Left-margin insertion reads roughly: 'donc ∪X_j^{0'} = X_i, d'autre part ∪X_j^0 = X_i par hyp. sur 𝔛_i' ('par hyp.' rather than 'ja').
The 'Je dis que' line is an insertion replacing the struck 'Cette réunion...'.

The whole block from 'On a donc prouvé par là-même X_j^{0'} ⊂ X_j^0' through 'les cellules ouvertes sont les X_j^0. En même temps, si j,k≤i, je dis que' is struck through with diagonal lines. The text that is not struck begins at 'Soient i,j∈I tels que X_i ⊂ X_j, prouvons i ≤ j. Soit x ∈ X_i^0 (X_i^0 ≠ ∅ par b')'.
